title: Modi to Visit Canada December 11-12 to Advance Trade and Strategic Ties
excerpt: India's High Commission in Ottawa confirmed the December 11-12 visit after Modi and Mark Carney spoke, with a CEPA trade deal, energy and people-to-people ties at the top of the agenda.
body:
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Canada on December 11-12, 2026, India's High Commission in Ottawa announced.
  • Modi and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney want concrete outcomes on trade, energy, technology, security and people-to-people ties.
  • Both leaders are committed to concluding a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement at the earliest opportunity, with an earlier ambition to lift bilateral trade toward CAD 70 billion by 2030.
  • For Canada's large Indian-origin community, the visit on December 11-12 is the clearest sign yet that the diplomatic reset is producing a working agenda.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Canada on December 11 and 12, 2026, the High Commission of India in Ottawa announced in a post on X, as reported by The Hindu. The announcement followed a recent conversation between Modi and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, in which both leaders agreed to build on positive momentum and work toward concrete outcomes across trade, energy, technology, security and people-to-people ties.

Reuters reported that Carney's office confirmed the December visit on Tuesday and said the two leaders had agreed to remain in close contact ahead of it.

Trade Deal at the Centre

The centrepiece is trade. Both governments say they are committed to concluding negotiations on a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement, or CEPA, at the earliest opportunity. A CEPA would set the rules for market access and investment between the two economies, and officials have previously set an ambition of expanding bilateral trade substantially by 2030, including a CAD 70 billion target cited in coverage of the leaders' earlier commitments.

https://x.com/narendramodi/status/2110355251840831509

The timing is deliberate. Canada's High Commissioner Christopher Cooter told The Hindu in September that the trade deal would be ready by the end of the year and that increased engagement through 2026 was intended to culminate in a December visit by Modi. Both leaders also welcomed a Team Canada Trade Mission to India led by International Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu, a signal that business engagement is moving ahead of the leaders' meeting.

Energy, Technology and Security

Beyond trade, the agenda spans energy, critical minerals, technology and innovation, and security cooperation. Canada is a major energy and minerals supplier, while India is one of the world's fastest-growing large markets for both. The two sides have also resumed higher-level engagement between national security and law enforcement officials after a difficult period in relations, and have discussed Indo-Pacific stability and Russia's war in Ukraine.

That breadth matters because the relationship had been defined for several years by diplomatic friction rather than delivery. A visit structured around signed or near-signed outcomes, rather than statements alone, would mark a change in kind, not just tone.

What It Means for the Diaspora

Canada hosts one of the largest Indian-origin populations in the world, and people-to-people ties were listed explicitly among the five areas the leaders discussed. Students, skilled workers, and families split between the two countries are directly affected by how smoothly the two governments handle education, migration and consular issues. Readers planning around the visit should note the dates, December 11-12, and watch for announcements on trade, student and work pathways, and direct business missions in the weeks before it.

A Busy December

The Canada stop is part of a dense diplomatic calendar. The Hindu reported Modi is expected to travel onward to the United States for the G20 summit from December 13 to 15, and then to Brussels from December 16 to 17, where he is expected to sign the EU free trade agreement and hold bilateral talks. Union Minister Piyush Goyal also said the first tranche of an India-U.S. trade deal was nearing final legal drafting.

Whether December delivers a signed CEPA will be the test of the reset. The visit dates are now fixed; the work of negotiators in the next eight weeks will decide what Modi and Carney have to announce when they meet.
